Insoluble ﬁber Dietary ﬁber resistant to digestion and insoluble in cold and hot water. Some may be partially degraded by
colonic bacteria
Monosaccharides A single sugar molecule (e.g., glucose, galactose, fructose)
Oligosaccharides Small polymers with from 3 to 20 two sugar units
Polysaccharides Large polymers of many sugar units such as starch or cellulose
Resistant starch Starches that escape digestion in the upper gastrointestinal tract. Five types have been identiﬁed
Short-chain fatty acids (SCFA) Metabolically active fatty acids with few carbons that are byproducts of bacterial fermentation
of food components in the colon (e.g., acetic, propionic, and butyric acids)
Sodium-linked glucose transporter (SGLT) Carriers using active transport (ATP-requiring) to carry glucose (and galactose)
across the mucosa and through the membrane
